audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit required equity capital for the receivables book
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 net receivable investment of $178.874 million less $36.260 million of net credit-facility borrowing equals $142.614 million before merchant-funding and other working-capital effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Required equity-funded receivables reinvestment would reduce owner earnings and the DCF anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash outflows for investing activities were from purchases and originations of notes receivable, net of repayments; purchasing computer equipment; and payments of salaries to employees who create capitalized internal-use software.
audit_findings.explanation: The $130.3 million anchor is approximately 2025 net income less software and equipment capex, so its omission of loan-book cash investment is demonstrated. The filing also demonstrates substantial receivables investment not matched by incremental borrowing. The record does not establish how much of the $142.614 million residual was recurring maintenance capital rather than temporary growth or timing, but the candidate amount exceeds the entire anchor and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a 2021-2026 funding schedule reconciling net receivable investment, net facility borrowing, merchant funding, credit losses and seasonal balances; determine normalized equity capital required at each forecast growth rate and rerun every scenario after deducting it from OE.

audit_findings.title: The anchor capitalizes a potentially non-durable surge in regulated consumer fees
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 late-payment fees of $74.0 million, up $48.8 million from $25.2 million in 2024
audit_findings.mechanism: Any normalization of consumer fees reduces the OE anchor; regulatory or collection constraints also reduce forecast growth and terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Consumer late payment fees totaled $74.0 million and $25.2 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The elevated fee pool and its $48.8 million annual increase are demonstrated, while its non-durability is unresolved. The $74.0 million fee pool equals 56.8% of the $130.3 million OE anchor before associated losses and taxes. Because even the bear case perpetuates the full anchor, a substantial reversal could materially lower all scenario values despite continued consumer-income growth reported in 2026.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 and 2026 consumer-fee revenue and associated credit losses by fee type, state and product; rerun the DCF under explicit fee-price, collectibility and regulatory-reversal stresses using normalized after-tax OE.

audit_findings.title: Credit-loss estimates could materially overstate the earnings numerator
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated allowance or provision inflates net income and OE; worse seasoned losses would also reduce sustainable margins and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We identified the allowance for credit losses for notes receivable as a critical audit matter given the subjective nature associated with the estimation of the historical loss rate assumption.
audit_findings.explanation: The allowance's estimation uncertainty is demonstrated, but an underprovision is not. The auditor identified the historical loss-rate assumption as subjective, while 2025 provision expense was already $89.298 million, or 68.5% of the OE anchor. June 2026 filings show continued provisioning and charge-offs but do not supply a vintage backtest sufficient to calculate any shortfall. The exposure is potentially material, but the record cannot establish its magnitude or confirm an error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain semi-monthly vintage roll-rate backtests through final charge-off, compare actual losses with the allowances recorded at each prior reporting date, isolate post-underwriting-change vintages and delinquency-fee receivables, and rerun OE for any demonstrated provision shortfall.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include operating or structurally trapped cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $79.757 million, equal to $2.26 per diluted share; $17.694 million was held by the VIE
audit_findings.mechanism: Only genuine excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; operating, collateral, settlement or customer-related cash should be excluded.
audit_findings.evidence: Our cash and cash equivalents were held primarily for working capital requirements and the continued investment in our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the cash is held primarily for working capital and investment, but it does not quantify the genuinely excess portion. Even removing the entire $79.757 million add-back would reduce values by only $2.26 per share, producing approximately $43.98, $51.95 and $61.29 for bear, base and bull versus the $120.58 market price. Thus this finding cannot by itself change the valuation conclusion, although the bridge should still be corrected for precision.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile unrestricted parent cash, VIE cash, settlement liquidity, customer funds and covenant or collateral minimums; replace the bridge add-back with verified excess cash and update the per-share outputs.

audit_findings.title: A share-price-driven tax benefit is embedded in peak OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.653 million tax benefit; 4.3% of the $130.3 million anchor and approximately $1.92-$2.68 per share of scenario value if removed
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing a nonrecurring tax benefit lowers after-tax OE and therefore operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The primary driver of the effective tax rate for the year ended December 31, 2025 related to $5.7 million of excess tax benefits on equity based compensation.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefit is demonstrably embedded because the anchor closely tracks 2025 net income less conventional capex, without a stated tax normalization. Eliminating all $5.653 million would reduce the anchor by about 4.3% and, because operating value scales with the anchor, reduce bear, base and bull values by approximately $1.92, $2.27 and $2.68 per share. Each result remains far below the $120.58 market price, so this item alone does not change the conclusion. The 2026 filing also reports further excess tax benefits, but durability remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized cash taxes excluding excess equity-compensation deductions, document any defensible recurring amount, and rerun the scenarios with the normalized after-tax anchor.

audit_findings.title: Public-benefit duties weaken the assumption that all residual economics are managed solely for common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Stakeholder-directed spending or foregone opportunities could reduce distributable OE or growth, while mission-related benefits could support retention, reputation or revenue.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, we may take actions that we believe will be in the best interests of those stakeholders materially affected by our specific benefit purpose, even if those actions do not maximize our financial results, and we may be restricted from pursuing certain growth opportunities to the extent not consistent with our public benefit corporation status.
audit_findings.explanation: The legal duty and potential conflict with shareholder maximization are demonstrated, but no incremental recurring expenditure, foregone project or restricted distribution is quantified. Existing public-benefit activities are already reflected in reported expenses and OE. Any additional valuation effect therefore depends on future board decisions rather than a presently demonstrated omission.
audit_findings.action: Monitor board-approved public-benefit budgets, capital-allocation decisions, foregone opportunities, distributions and biennial benefit reports; reserve recurring spending or adjust growth only when a separately measurable shareholder cost is documented.
